liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **What's Become Of The Baby** (1 review): Reviewer calls the original version of this song a highlight of the mix [6]
- **Cosmic Charlie** (1 review): Reviewer is especially fond of Cosmic Charlie, along with Doin' That Rag, in this original mix [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Rosemary**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]
- **Mountains of the Moon**: rare: 14 archived performances [14]
- **What's Become Of The Baby**: rare: 3 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-06-20.gd.aoxomoxoa.32074.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 8 songs; 38 min; rated 3.07/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this mix sounds sloppy and unfinished, with lyrics harder to hear than on the remixed version [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer notes Deadlists places the band in NYC on this date, and dead.net played from it as Jam of the Week; asks the true date [2]
- Reviewer argues this is a studio outtake, not a live show, and doubts it was ever released like this [8]
- Reviewer says the Dead played the Fillmore East on this date with Savoy Brown and Buddy Miles Express, and Aoxomoxoa was recorded in January [13]
- Reviewer finds this original mix far better than the 1971 remix, citing the two versions of St. Stephen [5]
- Reviewer says the rare 1969 mix differs markedly from the 1971 remix, and wonders why the original skipped the 2001 reissue [7]
- Reviewer says this alternate mix is famous and sought after, though whether it's better is subjective [11]
- Reviewer thinks the original mix is wilder than the later cleaned-up version and better reflects the period [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-06-20.gd.aoxomoxoa.32074.sbefail.shnf**: source: Ampex 16-track tape > LP > 24-bit, 44.1 kHz WAV > 16-bit, 44.1 kHz WAV > SHN [1]. Also: Reviewer says the original mix was officially issued in the 5LP Warner Bros Studio Albums boxset reissue; Reviewer says this is the mix first issued with the album; Garcia remixed it in 1971, and later releases used that until the boxset; Uploader says this is the original Aoxomoxoa mix, released commercially between June 1969 and late 1971 [1][6][9]
